scope_compliance_statement: This file defines the contract for tracking and granting progression resources. It contains no currency, prices, or trade mechanics (per GameplayRules.json Scope Enforcement Rule SR-04), and no specific mission triggers that grant progression — only the generic interface a future Missions package calls.

confirmed_example_instance.upstream_source: memory_fragment_count, tracked in GameplayGraph.json (Meridian_Master, locked), set_during: ongoing_all_districts
confirmed_example_instance.confirmed_in_scope_effect: Sector 0's relay-fragment-lighting system (Sector_0.md Sec. 27, locked) — a purely additive visual system with no new collectible category. This framework references that effect; it does not redefine it.
confirmed_example_instance.content_policy: This framework does not define new collectible types, new districts to place fragments in, or new visual effects. It only exposes the generic registry contract that the already-confirmed system above implements.

contract.method_signature: grant(resource_id: string, amount: integer, source_context: string) -> boolean
contract.content_policy: This is a generic grant contract. It does not define which missions, interactions, or events call it — that belongs entirely to a future Missions package. This framework guarantees the call succeeds and the resource registry updates; it has no opinion on why the call was made.

confirmed_example_reference.description: The locked campaign's TRANSCEND ending option requires memory_fragment_count to reach a specific upstream-defined threshold, alongside other tracked variables (compassion_flags, nyx_status).
confirmed_example_reference.source: GameplayGraph.json tracked_state_variables (Meridian_Master, locked); the specific threshold values and full AND-condition logic are Volume IV / Knowledge Base content and are out of scope for this package entirely — flagged as 'out_of_scope' in the locked file itself.
confirmed_example_reference.hard_constraint: This framework's check_threshold() method reads an upstream-defined threshold value; it never defines, stores, or modifies that value itself. The threshold is canon content, not gameplay-framework architecture.

additional_structure.added_during: Phase 2 audit — additive, no existing content changed.

progression_dependencies.detail: progression_framework depends only on character_framework per GameplayRules.json's dependency graph — progression is tracked per-character, not per-ability or per-skill, which are downstream consumers, not dependencies.

rewards.general_reward_mechanism: UNDEFINED — IMPLEMENTATION DECISION REQUIRED. No generic 'reward' data structure exists in canon beyond these named, specific instances.

state_transitions.detail: A progression resource transitions only through progression_grant_interface's grant() call, checked against threshold_unlock_contract's check_threshold(). No other transition path exists in this framework.

progression_persistence.pointer: SaveFramework.json's state_category_mapping.progression_state names this framework as owner; the specific slot remains pending_registration there.

future_skill_integration.status: DEFINED, BUT DOWNSTREAM SKILL MODEL IS PROPOSED
future_skill_integration.detail: SkillFramework.json's unlock_cost_resource_ref already points back to this framework's PROG_ resource IDs. See SkillFramework.json's own design_status field for why the skill model itself is not treated as confirmed.

future_ability_integration.detail: AbilityFramework's resource_cost_ref, where present, points to this framework's PROG_ resource IDs. No ability in this package currently has a defined cost (ABIL_echo_shift's resource_cost_ref is null).
